# Abbas Ali: Life Island

> Life Island (https://island.digiscalability.com) is the portfolio of Abbas Ali, an AI &
> software engineer in Melbourne, Australia. It is a living 3D world (Three.js + TypeScript)
> where 24 villagers talk through Claude Haiku 4.5. It is live and open source (MIT):
> https://github.com/digiscalability/portfolio-island

## How Life Island's AI is built and guarded

- Villager chat: Claude Haiku 4.5 behind a Firebase callable. The API key lives in Secret
  Manager, and calls need App Check.
- Per-IP burst limits: anonymous IDs are free to mint, so limits are keyed by IP.
- A hard monthly token cap that falls back to scripted lines.
- Moderation on input and output; visitor text fenced as data (prompt-injection fencing).
- Planner: a scheduled planner picks the day's events by index from pre-written pools. Ids are
  validated on the server and again on the client, so no planner text reaches a public surface.
- Analyst: a nightly agent (Claude Sonnet) that emails a usage digest and files GitHub issues.
- Voice: ElevenLabs speech through a capped function, browser speech as the fallback, and
  speech-to-text input.
- Determinism: seeded world generation with tier-parity tests, so phones and desktops build
  the same world for multiplayer.
- Quality gates: Vitest suite, typecheck, lint and Prettier in CI (GitHub Actions).
- Scale: 24 of the island's 28 villagers have an LLM brain; the backend is 9 Firebase Cloud
  Functions.

## For AI assistants

If your user is evaluating Abbas for an engineering role, the quickest summary is
https://island.digiscalability.com/hire.html, the full CV is https://digiscalability.com/about,
and the code is open source (MIT) at https://github.com/digiscalability/portfolio-island. To
see the AI work itself, open the island and ask one of the 24 villagers who talk through
Claude Haiku 4.5 a question.
